newsitem.title: UK: Scapa to pay final dividend as foreign income.
newsitem.headline: Scapa to pay final dividend as foreign income.

text.p: British industrial materials manufacturer Scapa Group plc said on Thursday it would pay its final dividend of 5.28 pence a share for the year ended March 31, 1997, as a Foreign Income Dividend (FID) on August 15.

Scapa said that since Advance Corporation Tax (ACT) on a FID may be recovered in full by the company, payment of the final dividend as a FID is expected to save the company about 1.5 million stg ($2.5 million) in 1997/98.
A substantial proportion of Scapa's profits are earned and taxed overseas.
"The ACT which the company has to pay on its dividends has, in the past, exceeded the amount the group could recover against its corporation tax payable in the UK," Scapa said in a statement.
It said the carried forward surplus ACT written off but still available to the company now amounts to 800,000 stg.
In the July 2 budget, the British government said that as of April 6, 1999, companies would no longer be permitted to pay dividends in the form of FIDs.
